content:
OSKAR HADDAD-LINDQVIST
Full-Stack Developer | React, TypeScript, Node.js
oskar.hl@example.com | +46 70 555 0808 | GitHub: oskarhl-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Full-stack developer with 12+ years of professional web development experience and a particular strength in frontend development. Experienced in building customer-facing applications with React, TypeScript, Node.js and SQL, with a focus on accessibility, performance and reliable delivery. Fluent in English.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Fullstack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | 2021–Present
- Build customer onboarding and KYC features in a six-person cross-functional team using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL.
- Built a BankID identity verification flow using a provider SDK, including QR-code and same-device flows, error handling and retries. A/B testing preceded a full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Built document upload using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in AWS Lambda, and scan status updates through SQS and PostgreSQL.
- Improved mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds through code splitting, image optimisation and dependency changes. Used Next.js server-side rendering for marketing pages.
- Addressed WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit findings in the onboarding flow and collaborated with designers using Figma.
- Helped migrate the backend incrementally from Express to NestJS and the frontend from Create React App to Vite. Maintained a GraphQL BFF with another developer.
- Deployed using AWS ECS Fargate and GitHub Actions; used Jest, Playwright, Docker, Storybook and Unleash. Participated in on-call rotations.
- Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024, conducting one-to-ones and sprint planning. Interviewed approximately 30 candidates.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | 2018–2021
- Built websites and web applications for approximately 25 clients using Angular, React, Node.js, Express, Laravel and WordPress.
- Led a two-developer ferry ticket app project and built most of the React Native app, which reached approximately 50,000 downloads. The app supported ticket purchase and offline ticket display.
- Set up GitLab CI for the agency, replacing an FTP-based deployment workflow.

Web Developer | Nordkust Media AB | 2014–2018
- Developed newspaper websites using PHP, jQuery and MySQL, and an article editor using AngularJS.
- Built a paywall integration and worked on Varnish caching and Ubuntu server administration.

Freelance Web Developer | 2012–2014
- Built websites for individuals and local businesses using PHP, jQuery and WordPress.

EDUCATION
Bachelor in Computer Science | West Coast University College, Gothenburg | 2011–2014

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Next.js, Angular, React Native, Storybook, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility fixes
Backend and data: Node.js, NestJS, Express, REST, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Prisma, PHP, Laravel
Cloud and delivery: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS and CloudWatch; Docker; GitHub Actions; GitLab CI
Testing and monitoring: Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest, Sentry, Datadog
Other: Figma, Agile/Scrum, A/B testing, BankID

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
- Mentor at a coding bootcamp, 2019–2020.
- Speaker at a local JavaScript meetup, 2022: “Migrating Express to NestJS without stopping the world.”

LANGUAGES
Swedish: Native | English: Fluent | Arabic: Spoken

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear chronology, relevant technical depth, and several quantified achievements. The most persuasive evidence is the onboarding conversion increase from 61% to 74%, mobile LCP improvement from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds, the 50,000-download mobile app, and the documented AWS, testing, accessibility, and delivery experience. The CV is professional and substantially more focused than the original candidate information. It could be marginally stronger by making a few job-specific capabilities more explicit, particularly Git-based workflows, web-security practices, semantic HTML/responsive UI work, and collaboration in design or usability-oriented processes. No material hallucinations or unsupported claims were detected when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, conventional reverse chronology, plain-text formatting, recognizable technology names, and a strong concentration of terms from the advertisement: React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, accessibility, WCAG, Jest, Playwright, AWS, Docker, Storybook, Next.js, and A/B testing. Its likely ATS and AI-screening probability is high because the core stack and outcomes are easy to identify. Minor keyword gaps are that Git itself is not named explicitly, semantic HTML and responsive layouts are not stated, and security-related experience is described through implementation details rather than terms such as authentication, secure uploads, or web security. These should only be made more explicit using the candidate's existing evidence; unsupported OWASP, GDPR, healthcare, or privacy claims should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent for the core role. The document clearly shows more than 2 years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js and SQL development, NestJS, PostgreSQL, automated unit and end-to-end testing, AWS, Docker, Next.js server-side rendering, Storybook, accessibility work, performance optimization, design collaboration, and A/B testing. The fintech/KYC context is relevant evidence of working with identity verification and sensitive customer data, although it is not healthcare experience. The candidate's material does not establish German or Croatian customer-facing proficiency. Health-data privacy and healthcare-specific requirements are not demonstrated, so these remain role-related gaps rather than defects in the CV. The CV also does not explicitly mention semantic HTML, responsive layouts, or formal OWASP knowledge, although it does show related frontend, mobile-performance, identity-verification, document-upload, and malware-scanning work.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Technical Skills section under “Cloud and delivery,” change “AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS and CloudWatch; Docker; GitHub Actions; GitLab CI” to “Git, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, AWS ECS/Fargate, S3, Lambda, SQS and CloudWatch; Docker.” This makes the Git-based workflow requirement explicit while remaining supported by the candidate’s GitHub Actions and GitLab CI experience.
2. In the Älvgrind Fintech experience, revise the document-upload bullet to make the security controls easier for an ATS and recruiter to recognize: “Built secure document upload using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV malware scanning in AWS Lambda, and scan-status updates through SQS and PostgreSQL.” Do not add OWASP, GDPR, or authentication claims that are not documented in the candidate information.
3. In the Professional Summary, replace the generic phrase “with a focus on accessibility, performance and reliable delivery” with “with a focus on accessible, high-performance customer-facing experiences, automated testing and reliable delivery.” This better mirrors the advertised emphasis while remaining supported by the WCAG fixes, LCP improvement, Jest/Playwright use, and production delivery experience.
4. In the Technical Skills section, change “WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility fixes” to “Web accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA audit remediation” and retain “HTML” and “CSS” in the same subsection. This presents the accessibility evidence more naturally and improves keyword clarity without claiming unsupported WCAG 2.2 expertise.
5. In the Älvgrind experience, revise “Addressed WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit findings in the onboarding flow and collaborated with designers using Figma” to “Remediated WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility-audit findings in the onboarding flow and collaborated with designers in Figma.” The revised wording is more concise and more closely matches the job’s accessibility and design-review emphasis.
6. In the Älvgrind experience, retain the explicit “mobile” wording in the performance bullet and consider changing “Improved mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds” to “Improved mobile Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds.” This preserves the metric while making the performance keyword easier to parse.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "with a focus on ... reliable delivery" — the candidate's material supports deployment, CI, testing and production work, but does not state that reliable delivery is a particular focus or achievement.
- "local businesses" — the source material names one local bakery; it does not support the plural claim about local businesses.
unsupported_claims: "with a focus on ... reliable delivery" — the candidate's material supports deployment, CI, testing and production work, but does not state that reliable delivery is a particular focus or achievement.
"local businesses" — the source material names one local bakery; it does not support the plural claim about local businesses.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from web developer to full-stack developer, relevant technical depth, and several quantified achievements. The strongest evidence is the 61% to 74% onboarding conversion improvement, LCP reduction from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds, approximately 50,000 app downloads, and leadership/interviewing experience. The document is concise and professional, and it avoids unsupported claims found in the original candidate information. The main content limitation is that some relevant capabilities are implied through tools and project descriptions rather than stated in the job description's terminology, particularly the distinction between automated testing types and the security/privacy context.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very good. The document uses conventional section headings, standard reverse-chronological experience formatting, searchable technology names, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting that would impair parsing. It contains the core keywords React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, SQL, AWS, Docker, GitHub Actions, Jest, Playwright, accessibility, WCAG, Storybook, Next.js, and A/B testing. AI screening probability is high because the recent experience closely matches the advertised stack and responsibilities, with especially strong evidence for React/TypeScript, Node.js/PostgreSQL, accessibility remediation, performance, testing, and cloud delivery. Minor ATS gains are possible by using the exact title spelling “Full-Stack Developer” and making automated testing activity more explicit rather than listing testing tools only within a deployment bullet.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is an excellent match for the role's core requirements. It shows substantially more than the required two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js and SQL development, accessibility work, automated testing, Git workflows, AWS, Docker, Storybook, Next.js, and A/B testing. The fintech KYC, identity-verification, secure document-upload, malware-scanning, and audit-remediation work is particularly relevant to Verdane Care's emphasis on privacy by default and responsible handling of sensitive data, although it is not healthcare experience specifically. The candidate also demonstrates work in a small cross-functional team, collaboration with designers, sprint planning, mentoring, and customer-facing application performance. German or Croatian customer-facing capability is a gap: the original information says German is forgotten and does not mention Croatian. Health-data privacy experience is not shown, but this is a learning requirement in the advertisement rather than a document defect. Semantic HTML, responsive layouts, and explicit OWASP terminology are not directly stated, although HTML/CSS, mobile performance work, and security-related implementation are present.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the headline, change “Full-Stack Developer | React, TypeScript, Node.js” only if consistency is desired to “Full-Stack Developer | React, TypeScript, Node.js” and retain the hyphenated form consistently throughout the document. This matches the job title more closely.
2. In the Professional Experience section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, revise the bullet beginning “Deployed using AWS ECS Fargate...” to make the testing activity more explicit without adding unsupported claims: “Used Jest and Playwright for automated testing; deployed with AWS ECS Fargate and GitHub Actions; also used Docker, Storybook and Unleash and participated in on-call rotations.”
3. In the Technical Skills section, keep “HTML” and “CSS” together with the accessibility entry rather than leaving them only in the broad Frontend list. For example: “Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Next.js, Angular, React Native, Storybook; Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA audit remediation.” This makes the frontend and accessibility match easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.
4. In the Professional Summary, replace the repeated phrase “customer-facing” with a more role-specific summary that foregrounds the strongest match: “Full-stack developer with 12+ years of professional web development experience, strongest in frontend development, building accessible and high-performance customer-facing applications with React, TypeScript, Node.js and SQL. Experienced with automated testing, WCAG 2.1 AA remediation, AWS delivery and cross-functional product teams.”
